title: Dynamic burst throttle rewrite and customer escalation runflow
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced sudden denied bursts and unexplained reserved-pool shortfalls during interleaved surge windows. Investigation shows the autoscaler admission controller can oversuppress burst admission when heterogeneous GPU clouds and KV-cache churn coincide. This ticket captures the rewrite of the burst throttle logic to a composite, telemetry-driven admission policy, the short-term emergency hotfix to restore fair burst admission, and the customer escalation/runflow to communicate mitigations and RCA timeline.

Repro: Load generator replay of Customer-A traffic shape (90th percentile short spikes + baseline QPS) on a mixed GPU fleet reproduces denied burst events after sustained KV cache evictions. Root causes include: 1) headroom estimator double-counting preemptible capacity in multi-az scenarios; 2) admission window aligning with KV cache eviction causing transient memory pressure and slot eviction; 3) weight normalization bug that amplifies large-tenant throttling under credit scarcity.

Impact: Affected customers see increased tail latency and 429/503s for short-lived spikes. Revenue and SLA risk for Dedicated tenants flagged as high.

Mitigation (temporary): apply soft-headroom bump (+15%) for VIP tenants, introduce a 30s "slot preemption grace" to prevent immediate eviction during KV churn, and enable hosted-fallback routing for critical routes. These were rolled to canary region us-west-2 at 2026-03-13 21:00 UTC and reduced customer 429s by ~72% on the canary.

Planned fix (longer-term): Replace the single-threshold admission heuristic with a composite policy that considers predicted short-burst probability, KV-cache pressure metric, and available burst-credit ledger. Add gated canary rollout with per-tenant assert checks and a synthetic-eval suite. Enhance telemetry: per-tenant headroom time-series, admission decision traces, and a burst-decision histograms dashboard.

Communications: interim note sent to impacted customers; full RCA targeted with timeline below.

Add admission trace headers to API responses to aid post-deploy debugging

Plan follow-up postmortem meeting with SRE/Runtime/PM/Support on 2026-03-22
notes: Temporary mitigations reduced customer impact but didn't fix double-counting when a tenant spans heterogeneous AZs.
Telemetry gap: admission decisions currently not correlated with per-tenant KV cache eviction traces; adding correlation will be high priority.
Consider long-term: integrate predictive headroom (short-burst model) into autoscaler to pre-allocate micro-burst slots for large tenants with burst history.
If composite policy fails at scale, fallback plan is to enable aggressive hosted-routing for critical routes and schedule emergency capacity increase with sales/ops.
